about: The motion library: reusable animations (moves) for any brand. One entry per move. A move is in this file only if it has a working example in the gallery.

reel.does: Plays every move one after another. One file per brand: motion-<brand>.mp4.

families.type: How words and numbers arrive and change.
families.emphasis: Drawing the eye on a product screen.
families.transition: Getting from one scene to the next.
families.capture-pointer: Pointer styles drawn over a product capture (CaptureClip).
families.capture-effect: Click, hover and typing effects on a product capture.
families.capture-camera: Camera moves over a product capture, from tracks.json and hand-set cues.
families.capture-time: Speed ramps, freezes, jumps, rewinds, pins and loops, all through one time map.
families.capture-look: Look presets: one word sets the pointer, click, camera and pace of a capture.
families.capture-staging: Where the screen sits: frames and layouts around a product capture (CaptureShot, staging.tsx).
families.capture-product: Animations on the product, glued to tracked things (CaptureClip's emphasis, emphasis.tsx).
families.capture-sound: Interface sounds placed from a capture's event log (sound.ts, tools/audio/capture_sounds.mjs).
families.capture-transition: Transitions between two captures, or two parts of one, on one film clock (CaptureJoin, transitions.tsx; the plan is joins.ts).
families.capture-relayout: A wide capture re-laid out for 9:16, 1:1 and 4:5, the camera following the action inside the recording; a phone-size take full frame (relayout.ts, CaptureShot in a tall or square frame).

moves.name: blur-in
moves.does: Each word of a headline is there, soft, at once; it reaches its place first and comes into focus last.
moves.use_when: Calm films, and headlines that should arrive gently.
moves.avoid_when: Fast or hype passages, and any line that must be read the instant it appears.

props.lines: One or two clauses. The first is in ink, the second in the second colour. Star one word to set it in the accent voice.
props.at: Seconds on the scene clock when the move starts.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: tracking-settle
moves.does: The letters of one line start a little wider apart and close up, from rest, slowing into the brand's own spacing.
moves.use_when: The opening line or the closing line of a film.
moves.avoid_when: Sentences in the middle of a film, and more than one line at a time.

props.at: Seconds on the scene clock when the move starts.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: rotating-word
moves.does: The last word of a line swaps for another inside a box that resizes to fit, while the rest of the line holds still. The words are on one roll: the old one leaves through the top as the new one comes up, and nothing fades.
moves.use_when: One line that is true for several audiences or uses.
moves.avoid_when: More than four words in the rotation, or when the changing word is not the last on the line.

props.lead: The words before the box. Optional.
props.words: Two or more words, shown one at a time.
props.at: Seconds when the line and its first word arrive.
props.every: Seconds each word stays, taken from the voice: about half a second of reading plus the swap.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: number-roll
moves.does: The digits of a number roll to their value in fixed-width figures, the last digit landing last. A number that arrives comes up from empty through a few digits per wheel, blurred while fast; it never spins a full turn and never shows a leading zero.
moves.use_when: Prices, counts and percentages, and a value that updates from an old number to a new one.
moves.avoid_when: Numbers that must be compared with a bar or a ring (use count-with-bar), and an old value that is longer than the new one.

props.at: Seconds when the roll starts. It ends one scene length later.
props.from: The old value, on screen before the roll. Optional. Without it the number arrives rolling.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.prefix: Text before the number, such as a currency sign. Optional.
props.unit: Text after the number at 60% of its size, such as %. Optional.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: type-on
moves.does: Characters appear at a human rhythm: bursts of a few letters, with small pauses at spaces and punctuation.
moves.use_when: Prompts and search fields in product UI.
moves.avoid_when: Film headlines, and long text that nobody needs to watch being typed.

props.at: Seconds when the first key is pressed.
props.over: Seconds the typing takes in all. Optional. A prompt takes 2 to 3 seconds whatever its length.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.caret: Show the caret, a line in the accent colour. Optional; on by default.
props.seed: A number that picks the rhythm. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: swap-word
moves.does: One word rolls out through the top of the line and its replacement rolls in from below, while the rest of the line holds. The two are never printed over each other.
moves.use_when: Before and after in one line.
moves.avoid_when: More than one swap in a line, or when the swapped word is not the last on its line.

props.lead: The words before the swapped word. Optional.
props.from: The old word, in the warm colour.
props.to: The new word, in the accent.
props.at: Seconds when the line arrives.
props.swapAt: Seconds when the word is swapped.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: drawn-mark
moves.does: An underline, or a ring drawn as a hand draws one (a little square, a little uneven, its end passing outside its start), is drawn on its child in the accent colour.
moves.use_when: Pointing at one word, number or control without adding text.
moves.avoid_when: With another emphasis on the same beat (a lift, a focus pull), or more than one mark on screen at once.

props.children: The word, number or control to mark.
props.at: Seconds when the mark is drawn: an underline in a quick length, a ring in a base length.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.weight: Thickness of the stroke as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.gap: Space between the child and an underline, as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: focus-pull
moves.does: Everything except the chosen child dims and softens.
moves.use_when: One thing in a group matters for this beat.
moves.avoid_when: More than five things in the group, or with another emphasis on the same beat.

props.children: The group. Each child sits in a box of its own.
props.keep: Which child stays sharp, counting from 0.
props.at: Seconds when focus is pulled.
props.out: Seconds when focus is given back. Optional.
props.style: CSS that lays the group out. Optional.
props.itemStyle: CSS for each child's box. Optional.

moves.name: lift
moves.does: A card rises off the surface: it grows 2 to 3% and its shadow grows and softens. On a dark page, where a shadow hardly shows, it also catches light along its top edge and rim and a soft glow of the accent spreads under it.
moves.use_when: A selected card or row, on either page.
moves.avoid_when: With another emphasis on the same beat.

props.children: The card. Give it no shadow of its own.
props.at: Seconds when it lifts.
props.out: Seconds when it is set down again. Optional.
props.radius: Corner radius of the card as a percentage of frame height. Optional; the brand's window radius by default.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: stagger
moves.does: The items of a group arrive in order from a source: the left, the centre, or a point.
moves.use_when: Rows, tiles and lists arriving as a result.
moves.avoid_when: Groups of more than about twelve, and a single item.

props.children: The items. Each sits in a box of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the first item arrives.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.from: "left", "centre", or the position (counting from 0) of the item at the point, such as the one the cursor clicked. Optional; left by default.
props.columns: How many items per row, when the group is a grid. Optional.
props.style: CSS that lays the group out. Optional.
props.itemStyle: CSS for each item's box. Optional.

moves.name: count-with-bar
moves.does: A number counts up while its bar grows. The last step of the count lands as the bar comes to rest.
moves.use_when: One number that matters, shown against a whole or a target.
moves.avoid_when: Several numbers at once, and a number with no meaningful maximum (use number-roll).

props.max: The value of a full bar.
props.at: Seconds when the label and the faint track arrive.
props.countAt: Seconds when the count and the bar start. Optional; just after the label by default.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.label: A short label above the number. Optional.
props.unit: Text after the number at 60% of its size. Optional.
props.width: Width as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

also_exports.Count: The counting number on its own, for the middle of a ring or beside a line. Props: value, at, from, over, decimals.

moves.name: bar-grow
moves.does: One bar grows from its baseline to its value and slows into place.
moves.use_when: Before against after, or a small chart of up to about six bars, each started a little after the last.
moves.avoid_when: Charts that need a legend, and bars that do not start at zero.

props.share: The bar's value as a share of the full length, 0 to 1.
props.at: Seconds when it starts to grow.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.length: Full length as a percentage of frame height.
props.thickness: Thickness as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.over: How long it grows: a timing token. Optional; base by default.
props.track: Show the full length, faint, before the bar arrives. Optional.
props.emphasis: Paint the bar in the accent: the one bar the chart is about. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: line-draw
moves.does: A line draws itself along a path, and its end mark appears last.
moves.use_when: Change over time as one line, or connecting two things on screen.
moves.avoid_when: Several lines at once, and before the viewer has seen both ends.

props.points: Two or more places the line passes through, in pixels of the frame.
props.at: Seconds when it starts to draw.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.over: How long it draws: a timing token. Optional; scene by default, base or quick for a connector.
props.curve: Draw one smooth curve through the points. Optional.
props.weight: Thickness as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.mark: Show the end mark, a short stroke across the end. Optional; on by default.
props.label: A value shown above the end when the line arrives, in the accent. Optional.

moves.name: ring-sweep
moves.does: A ring fills clockwise from the top to its share of a whole.
moves.use_when: A share of a whole, with its number in the middle.
moves.avoid_when: More than one ring on screen, and shares that need comparing with each other.

props.share: How much of the ring fills, 0 to 1.
props.at: Seconds when the sweep starts.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Diameter as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.weight: Thickness as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.over: How long it sweeps: a timing token. Optional; scene by default.
props.children: What sits in the middle, such as a Count with the same start. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: camera
moves.does: A wrapper that moves a whole shot one way: a slow drift, a push in on a point, or a follow behind the pointer. A push closes in at one steady rate, by a constant factor.
moves.use_when: Going from the whole window to the one element the beat is about, or keeping a held shot alive with a drift.
moves.avoid_when: More than one move in a shot (never in, out, in), and slow moves across small text.

props.children: The content of the shot. Keep the Stage outside it.
props.direction: For a drift: "in", "out", "up", "down", "left" or "right". Optional; in by default. Its size comes from the preset.
props.to: For a push or a follow: the point to go to, in pixels of the frame.
props.at: For a push: seconds when it starts. For a follow: seconds when the pointer clicks, which is when the camera lands.
props.scale: How far it zooms. Optional; at most 2.5.
props.over: For a push: "scene" or "hero". Optional; scene by default.

moves.technique_note: The follow move is technique 7, cursor lead; cursor-lead is that move with its cursor. Drift and push are moves inside a shot, not scene changes.

moves.name: container-transform
moves.does: A small card grows to become the whole frame, its content appearing in the last third; reversed, the frame shrinks back into the card.
moves.use_when: Going into a detail, or back out to the bigger picture.
moves.avoid_when: Twice in a row, and when the card and the next scene are on the same page colour as the stage.

props.children: The full-frame scene inside the container.
props.from: Where the small card sits: x, y, width and height in pixels of the frame.
props.at: Seconds when it starts to grow (or to shrink).
props.page: The brand page the container is painted in: "light" or "dark".
props.card: What the small card shows, such as a label. Optional.
props.reverse: Start full and shrink to the card. Optional.
props.radius: Corner radius of the card as a percentage of frame height. Optional.

moves.name: push-through
moves.does: The camera pushes into one element until its colour fills the frame, and that colour is the page of the next scene. What grows is a plain plate over the element; the rest of the outgoing scene softens and is gone before it is enlarged, and the next scene starts on the frame after the colour covers the frame.
moves.use_when: Entering a new world: product to brand, light to dark.
moves.avoid_when: The element has fine detail, or the two scenes are on the same page.

props.children: The outgoing scene, with the element in it.
props.next: The next scene. Its clock starts at 0 on the frame after the colour covers the frame.
props.target: The element to enter: x, y, width and height in pixels of the frame.
props.at: Seconds when the push starts.
props.page: The brand page of the element and of the next scene: "light" or "dark".
props.radius: Corner radius of the element as a percentage of frame height. Optional; the brand's control radius by default.

moves.planned_note: At 2.45 s the plate hands over to the page it has become; the picture does not change on that frame.

moves.name: relay-scroll
moves.does: The outgoing content speeds up and off, blurring along its way, is swapped in one frame, and the incoming content starts a little low and slows to rest. No fade, and no empty page between.
moves.use_when: Moving to the next step in a sequence.
moves.avoid_when: Unrelated scenes, and changing direction between steps of one film.

props.next: The incoming content. Its clock starts at 0 on the swap; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing content starts to leave.
props.reach: How far the outgoing content must travel to be out of the frame, as a share of the frame: 1 for content that fills it, about 0.6 for a line or a card in the middle. Optional; 1 by default.

moves.name: zoom-through-swap
moves.does: The outgoing group shrinks, speeding up, and dissolves over one tick into the next, which is already shrinking from large and slows to its size. It reads as one pull-back; there is no empty frame.
moves.use_when: A full change of content inside one world.
moves.avoid_when: Text that must be read during the swap, and next to another zoom.

props.next: The incoming group. Its clock starts at 0 as it appears, half a tick before the middle of the join; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing group starts to shrink.

moves.planned_note: The join at 2.11 s is a dissolve one tick long, not an instant change.

moves.name: slide-off-reveal
moves.does: Finished content speeds up and off one side, blurring along its way, while the next title, already beneath it, comes up.
moves.use_when: Ending a section and naming the next.
moves.avoid_when: The middle of a section, and when the next thing is not a title.

props.next: The title beneath. Give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the content starts to leave.

moves.name: light-sweep
moves.does: One soft band of light crosses a surface once. The band carries a faint wash of the accent, so it also shows on near-white cards.
moves.use_when: A reveal: the moment a result or a new state appears.
moves.avoid_when: More than once in a film, and on a loop.

props.children: The surface: a card, a window or a button.
props.at: Seconds when the band starts to cross.
props.radius: Corner radius of the surface as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: parallax-camera
moves.does: Three planes at different depths slide at different speeds as the camera moves: the far plane 35% as far as the product and out of focus, the near plane 150% as far.
moves.use_when: A camera move that should feel like a space: arriving at a product screen, or travelling across a workspace.
moves.avoid_when: The near plane would cross what is being read, and shots with nothing behind or in front of the product.

props.children: The product plane, laid out as it should be when the camera has arrived.
props.far: What sits far behind it, softened and dimmed. Optional.
props.near: A foreground detail in front of it. Optional. Keep it clear of what is read.
props.at: Seconds when the camera starts to move.
props.by: How far the product plane slides, as shares of the frame's width and height (x and y). The camera moves the other way.

moves.name: momentum-cut
moves.does: The outgoing shot starts to slide, speeding up; a hard cut; the incoming shot is already moving the same way, at the same speed, and settles in about 300 ms.
moves.use_when: Joining two zoom levels of the same screen (the whole view, then one element close up) without zooming across small text.
moves.avoid_when: The two shots are on different pages or in different worlds, and calm passages where a carried move would do.

props.next: The incoming shot. Its clock starts at 0 on the cut; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing shot starts to move. The cut is one quick length later.

moves.name: shared-element
moves.does: One element travels on a shallow arc from its place in one layout to its place in the next, changing size and corner radius. Its place sets off first and its size lands last; its text changes over only at the midpoint and is never stretched.
moves.use_when: Two layouts share one thing: a row that becomes a card, a button that becomes a header. The default way to change scene inside a product.
moves.avoid_when: The two layouts share nothing, and more than one shared element at a time.

props.from: Where the element is in the first layout: x, y, width and height in pixels of the frame.
props.to: Where it is in the second layout.
props.at: Seconds when it sets off. The move takes a base and a tick.
props.before: What it holds in the first layout, laid out at that size. Optional.
props.after: What it holds in the second layout, laid out at that size. Optional.
props.radius: Corner radius before and after, as percentages of frame height. Optional; the brand's control and window radii by default.
props.style: Extra CSS for the surface. Optional.

moves.name: cursor-lead
moves.does: A large cursor travels on an arc and clicks; the camera sets off a quick length after it, covers 70% of the way while pushing in, and lands with the click. Pressed, exported beside it, dips the control under the click.
moves.use_when: Tutorials and demos: the next thing happens where the cursor goes.
moves.avoid_when: No interaction is happening, and anything on screen that changes before the click.

props.children: The screen. Put the clicked control in a Pressed with the same at.
props.from: Where the cursor starts, in pixels of the frame.
props.to: The point it clicks, in pixels of the frame.
props.at: Seconds when it clicks, which is when the camera lands. Show the result one frame later.
props.scale: How far the camera pushes in. Optional.
props.bend: How far the cursor's path bows, as a share of the distance. Optional.
props.out: Seconds when the cursor leaves. Optional.

moves.name: icon-door
moves.does: An icon tile sits in front of a miniature of a live screen. The camera pushes through in about 600 ms as the tile slides away, and the miniature is the screen; run back, in about 850 ms, the screen shrinks to a card and the tile slides back over it.
moves.use_when: Entering and leaving an app or a feature from a menu, a hub or a dashboard.
moves.avoid_when: Any other meaning in the same film, and a screen that cannot be shown small without looking broken.

props.children: The screen behind the door, laid out at full size. Its clock starts at 0 on at, so it builds while the camera travels.
props.icon: What the tile shows, in the middle of it.
props.tile: Where the tile sits: x, y, width and height in pixels of the frame.
props.at: Seconds when the camera starts through.
props.back: Seconds when it comes back out. Optional.
props.around: The rest of the menu. It goes as the camera passes and returns on the way back. Optional.
props.page: The brand page of the screen, if it is not the page the menu is on. Optional.

moves.name: cursor-classic
moves.does: A clean, generic arrow with a soft shadow, about 1.5 times a real pointer, in the brand's pointer colours. It turns into a hand over buttons and a text bar over fields, and presses to 90% on each click.
moves.use_when: Most demos and tutorials.
moves.avoid_when: Films that want no pointer at all (use hidden).

moves.name: cursor-brand
moves.does: The same arrow filled with the brand's accent colour and a rounder, heavier outline.
moves.use_when: Branded launches and social cuts.
moves.avoid_when: Screens where the accent colour is everywhere already, so the pointer would get lost.

moves.name: cursor-dot
moves.does: A small solid dot with a light ring.
moves.use_when: Montages and calm films, where the pointer should hardly be noticed.
moves.avoid_when: Tutorials: a dot does not show where exactly the click lands.

moves.name: cursor-halo
moves.does: A small accent dot inside a soft ring of light.
moves.use_when: Dark product screens and dark stages.
moves.avoid_when: Light, busy screens, where the ring reads as a stain.

moves.name: cursor-spotlight
moves.does: The classic arrow lights a soft circle around itself while the rest of the screen dims slightly.
moves.use_when: Busy screens where the eye needs guiding.
moves.avoid_when: Shots where something else on the screen must be read, and together with a focus pull (one emphasis per beat).

moves.name: cursor-presenter
moves.does: A larger arrow with a bold outline that still reads on a phone.
moves.use_when: Social cuts and tutorials watched on phones.
moves.avoid_when: Wide desktop films, where it looks oversized.

moves.name: cursor-named
moves.does: An accent arrow with a name tag, as in shared editors.
moves.use_when: Two-person and collaboration moments.
moves.avoid_when: Films with one person: a name tag invents a second user.

props.cursorName: The name on the tag, made up and safe to show.

moves.name: cursor-touch
moves.does: A soft see-through dot that presses down, with a ring on each tap and a short fading line while dragging.
moves.use_when: Phone-sized takes.
moves.avoid_when: Desktop takes: there is no finger on a desktop.

moves.name: cursor-hidden
moves.does: No pointer; the camera and the click effects lead.
moves.use_when: Cinematic shots and hero moments.
moves.avoid_when: Tutorials: people need to see where to click.

moves.name: click-ring
moves.does: A thin accent ring spreads from the click point and fades, starting as the button goes down.
moves.use_when: Most films: the default click.
moves.avoid_when: More than one click effect in a film.

moves.name: click-pulse
moves.does: A soft accent fill pulses over the button that was clicked (its tracked box), or a soft disc where nothing is tracked.
moves.use_when: Launches and demos where the button itself is the point.
moves.avoid_when: Small icons and dense rows, where the fill covers the neighbours.

moves.name: click-burst
moves.does: Eight short accent lines burst out from the click and fade. In a film that is not hype it becomes a ring.
moves.use_when: Hype films and social cuts.
moves.avoid_when: Calm and confident films.

moves.name: click-squish
moves.does: No mark on the screen: the pointer presses deeper (to 82%) and springs back.
moves.use_when: Films with sound on, where the click sound carries the moment.
moves.avoid_when: Sound-off social cuts: a squish alone is easy to miss.

moves.name: hover-magnet
moves.does: In the last fifth of a move the pointer is pulled onto its target a little faster, as if drawn in. The click still lands at the recorded place and time.
moves.use_when: Demos and launches.
moves.avoid_when: Calm and documentary films.

moves.name: hover-glow
moves.does: The tracked thing under a resting pointer gets a soft accent glow; it fades as the pointer moves on.
moves.use_when: Guiding the eye to the button about to be clicked.
moves.avoid_when: Untracked captures (nothing to glow), and beats that already carry another emphasis.

moves.name: typing-caret-glow
moves.does: The field being typed in glows with an accent edge that brightens on each key. The engine does not know the caret's exact place, so the whole field glows.
moves.use_when: Any typing worth watching.
moves.avoid_when: Pasted text that is not the point of the shot.

moves.name: typing-key-caps
moves.does: Shortcuts (or every key, in tutorials) show as key caps near the bottom of the screen; each cap presses as its key goes down.
moves.use_when: Shortcuts the viewer should learn.
moves.avoid_when: Ordinary typing: key caps for every letter are noise.

moves.name: camera-auto-zoom
moves.does: Before each action the camera eases in on the real thing it happens to (from tracks.json) with room around it, holds through the action and a proof moment, and eases out. Actions close in time and place share one shot. Never past 2x, never during a reading hold.
moves.use_when: Every demo: the default camera.
moves.avoid_when: Captures where the whole screen must stay in view, and documentary films.

moves.name: camera-follow
moves.does: While zoomed in, the camera drifts towards the pointer 150 ms behind it and covers 30% of the way, never so far that the thing leaves the shot.
moves.use_when: Demos with travel inside one zoomed area.
moves.avoid_when: Tutorials, where a steady frame is easier to follow.

moves.name: camera-push-in
moves.does: A slow move in on a thing, a click or a box, by hand.
moves.use_when: Landing a proof moment.
moves.avoid_when: Pushing in, out and in again in one shot.

moves.name: camera-pull-out
moves.does: Starts close on a detail and reveals the whole screen.
moves.use_when: Opening a scene on the result, then showing where it lives.
moves.avoid_when: Text that is being read while the camera moves.

moves.name: camera-snap-zoom
moves.does: A fast zoom with a tiny settle, for beats. In a film that is not hype it is an ordinary push in.
moves.use_when: Hype films, on a beat.
moves.avoid_when: Calm and confident films.

moves.name: camera-dolly-tilt
moves.does: The screen starts turned in depth (at most 10 degrees) and straightens as the camera moves in a little. Turns fade away as the camera closes in: wides only.
moves.use_when: Openings and wide establishing shots.
moves.avoid_when: Any screen that must be read while it is turned.

moves.name: camera-float
moves.does: The screen drifts very slowly in depth (about 2 degrees), alive through holds. Wides only.
moves.use_when: Launch hero shots and long holds on a wide screen.
moves.avoid_when: Tutorials and zoomed shots.

moves.name: camera-crane-reveal
moves.does: Starts tight on one thing and rises to the whole page, leaning back a little in depth on the way.
moves.use_when: Revealing the whole product after a detail.
moves.avoid_when: Short shots: it needs a hero length.

moves.name: camera-orbit
moves.does: A small turn around the floating screen, from one side to the other (at most 10 degrees). Wides only.
moves.use_when: Launch hero shots.
moves.avoid_when: Anything that must be read.

moves.name: camera-rack-focus
moves.does: One thing is sharp and the rest softens and dims; the sharp area moves to a second thing.
moves.use_when: Moving the eye from a cause to its result on one screen.
moves.avoid_when: Together with a spotlight pointer (one emphasis per beat).

moves.name: camera-pan-across
moves.does: A smooth slide across the screen at a set zoom, from one thing to another.
moves.use_when: Showing a long row of things, or two related places on one screen.
moves.avoid_when: Fast films: it needs a hero length.

moves.name: time-speed-ramp
moves.does: A long real wait (marked by the capture tool) or long typing plays faster, easing into and out of the faster speed, with a "Sped up" label in the brand's label style. The pointer, the tracked things and the camera follow the same clock.
moves.use_when: Any real wait over 0.6 s, and long typing.
moves.avoid_when: Waits that are the point of the story (show them, or cut them with a jump).

moves.name: time-freeze
moves.does: One moment of the recording holds while the camera pushes in slowly (5%), then eases back as the picture plays on.
moves.use_when: Proof moments: a result the viewer should believe.
moves.avoid_when: More than once or twice a film.

moves.name: time-jump
moves.does: A dead stretch is left out with a clean cut.
moves.use_when: Long waits where nothing changes on screen.
moves.avoid_when: Stretches where the pointer or the page is moving (the cut would show).

moves.name: time-rewind
moves.does: The recording runs backwards for a moment, easing in and out, then plays on from there or cuts back to where it was.
moves.use_when: Undo stories and "let us see that again".
moves.avoid_when: More than once a film.

moves.name: time-pin
moves.does: An event (a click, a mark, a step) lands on a chosen film time, such as a word of the voice. The pauses between actions are stretched or squeezed to fit; actions are never retimed.
moves.use_when: Fitting a capture to the voice.
moves.avoid_when: Pins that need the pauses to play more than 8 times faster or 4 times slower (the engine refuses, with a plain message).

moves.name: time-loop
moves.does: In its last stretch the clip dissolves back to its first frame while the camera and the pointer go back, so it can play in a loop.
moves.use_when: Social loops and website heroes.
moves.avoid_when: Films that end on a call to action.

review.about: Every move was watched frame by frame at 60 frames a second, fixed and rendered again before it was marked reviewed. "planned_instant_changes" lists, in seconds of the move's own preview, each change that is meant to happen in one frame (a cut or a swap), so tools/checks/smoothness.py can be given them with --planned-cuts and report only the unplanned ones.
review.known_limit: The browser places every line of text on a whole pixel from top to bottom. A slow vertical settle of text therefore ends in steps of one pixel at full size (two in half-size previews). Moves keep small overshoots off text for this reason.

shared.about: Helpers every move can use, exported from engine/src/kit/moves.
shared.MotionBlur: Wraps anything that moves fast and blurs it along its way, matched to its speed (half-frame shutter). Nothing blurs below reading speed. Give it x and y, the pixels travelled this frame.
shared.useTravel: Gives the pixels travelled this frame for any place written as a function of scene time.

capture.about: Entries in the capture families are settings of CaptureClip, not components of their own. Their previews play a stretch of a real capture chosen from its own events (engine/src/library/motion/capture.tsx); the compositions take a "capture" prop ("<job>/<id>", empty for the newest). Check them with tools/checks/capture_motion.mjs as well as tools/checks/smoothness.py.
capture.practice_page_note: Previews were rendered at half size from a practice capture whose search box opens and closes in one frame, with no animation of its own. Those one-frame changes are in the recording itself and are listed in planned_instant_changes (typing-key-caps, time-speed-ramp, time-jump); a preview made from another capture has other ones.
capture.staging_and_product: Stagings are CaptureShot (engine/src/kit/capture/staging.tsx), product animations are CaptureClip's emphasis (emphasis.tsx), glued through glue.ts. Their previews (engine/src/library/motion/product.tsx) take "capture", "second", "things" (fixed places for a take that tracked nothing), "roles" and "address". Rendered at half size 12 Nov 2026: Tulvo's boards take (with its cards given as things, measured from the marks) for most, a practice take where typing, a message, a scroll or a second take was needed. Check glue with tools/checks/capture_glue.mjs on a GlueProbe render; measure where the picture really scrolled first with tools/film/seen_scroll.mjs.
capture.transitions: Entries in the capture-transition family are CaptureJoin with one "transition" name. Their previews join the two parts of Tulvo's boards take 2 at the click on "Campaign Launch Board" (splitAtClick), rendered at half size with the props {"capture": "tulvo-capture-test/boards-take-2", "options": {"join": {"from": {"x": 12, "y": 381, "width": 223, "height": 33}}, "b": {"from": 7.25}}} (the link measured from the mark still; the second part starts after Tulvo's placeholders have gone); shared element adds "to": the breadcrumb title {"x": 365, "y": 17, "width": 151, "height": 19}. "second" names another take for the second part. The contact sheet is library/motion/transition-sheet.jpg. Check them with tools/checks/capture_transitions.mjs (pointer and clicked thing across the join, lengths) as well as tools/checks/smoothness.py and tools/checks/capture_motion.mjs.
capture.relayout: Entries in the capture-relayout family are CaptureShot in a 9:16, 1:1 or 4:5 frame: the staging is re-laid for the frame (relayout.ts, sizedStaging) and the camera follows the action inside the wide recording (planFollow), keeping the acted-on thing and the pointer inside the safe area with a margin on every frame. On 9:16 the safe area is the band Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts all leave free (top 14%, bottom 35%, right-hand buttons), less the caption slot. Previews (engine/src/library/motion/relayout.tsx, "move-relayout-<name>") were rendered at half size 12 Nov 2026 from Tulvo's boards take (take 5) with the link and the New button given as things from capture.json's step targets: {"capture": "tulvo-capture-test/boards", "things": {"link": {"rect": [12, 381.5, 223, 32], "from": 4.4, "to": 7.4}, "new": {"rect": [1807.7, 80, 80.3, 34], "from": 8.9}}}; the join adds {"options": {"join": {"from": {"x": 12, "y": 381, "width": 223, "height": 33}}, "b": {"from": 7.25}}}. The phone-size take previews use a stand-in (engine/public/jobs/_relayout-test/capture/phone-stand-in: the left 390 x 844 page pixels of the same take), not a real phone take. The contact sheet is library/motion/relayout-sheet.jpg.
